answer: A verifiable delay protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate sequential squarings along an unparallelizable spiral delay curve. An adversary attempting to mint fake identities must burn scarce single-core compute cycles and continuous electricity per node. Observers verify these proofs via compact falcon signatures anchored to an immutable marble ledger. However, this defense creates an asymmetric advantage for well-funded attackers possessing custom ASIC hardware.
